column1: # perl-suite-fixture.tsv — HARNESS-FIXTURE artifacts for tools/run-perl-suite.pl
# One row per file: <rel-path><TAB><failing test numbers, comma-separated><TAB><cause>
# WHAT BELONGS HERE, and why it is not perl-suite-expected.tsv (ruled s320,
# fable-answers-s318.md §10): a row here says the divergence is produced by the
# MEASUREMENT SETUP, not by PCL.  perl-suite-expected.tsv's bar is "explained by
# a blessed docs/not-supported.md section" — filing an artifact there would
# claim PCL lacks a feature it actually has, and a future reader would believe
# it.  So artifacts get their own status (FIXTURE) and their own file.
# THE BAR — higher than expected.tsv's, because "the harness did it" is the
# easiest excuse in the codebase to reach for:
#   1. Every primitive the failing rows exercise must be PROBED and shown to
#      behave identically in PCL and in perl.  "PCL looks right" is not enough.
#   2. The cause must name the specific piece of setup that differs, in one
#      line, with the session that established it.
#   3. If the fix is in PCL (a drifted shim, a missing builtin), it is NOT an
#      artifact — fix it.  See the RESOLVED list below for two that were.
# ENFORCEMENT (runner): rows are matched per TEST NUMBER against the per-test
# failure log, all-or-nothing.  One unregistered failing row and the file stays
# DIFF, naming the intruders — a real bug landing in a fixture-affected file
# can never hide behind the registration.  A registered file that starts fully
# passing is flagged STALE and FAILS the run, same as expected.tsv.
# file
op/chdir.t
column3: Task #172 (s319): the shadow t/ SYMLINKS op/, and getcwd(3) returns the PHYSICAL path, so the test's `"$Cwd/op"` can never equal the post-chdir cwd. perl runs in the real tree, PCL in the shadow. Probed identical in both: bare chdir() honouring HOME *and* LOGDIR, delete $ENV{}, cwd() tracking a chdir, rel2abs(curdir), and chdir-into-a-symlink resolving to the physical path. Nothing in PCL is wrong; the two sides run in different trees.
